WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050: Cross-sector Summary. Prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), London, March 2015. No DOI or report number printed. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/industrial-decarbonisation-and-energy-efficiency-roadmaps-to-2050

Cross-sector synthesis of the eight UK sector roadmaps (31 pages; UK, 2012 base year). No technology-level numbers: it holds sector pathway results only (Table 2: 2012 emissions, BAU and Max Tech reductions per sector, e.g. chemicals 18.4 Mt CO2 base, BAU 31%, Max Tech 79-88%; oil refining 16.3 Mt, BAU 44%, Max Tech 64%; food and drink 9.5 Mt, BAU 40%, Max Tech 66-75%), combined totals (81 Mt CO2 in 2012; 58 Mt BAU, 42 Mt intermediate and 22 Mt Max Tech in 2050), the share of each technology group in the combined reductions (Max Tech: carbon capture 37%, grid decarbonisation 25%, biomass 16%, energy efficiency and heat recovery 13%), an order-of-magnitude discounted capital cost (GBP 6 billion BAU to 16 billion Max Tech, 3.5% discount rate), the option-group categorisation (Table 1) and a list of lower-TRL options per sector (Table 3, no numbers). The technology option registers with TRL, capex and savings are in the sector appendices (extracted separately: chemicals wsp_2015_004, oil refining wsp_2015_005, food and drink wsp_2015_006; cement, ceramic, glass, iron and steel, pulp and paper by other extractions).
